title: Ranking and Partitioning of Attention Heads for Sparse and Continual Reinforcement Learning Fine-tuning
abstract: arXiv:2610.21336v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study sparse and continual reinforcement learning fine-tuning of language models through attention-head ranking and partitioning. For sparse learning, we rank attention heads by gradient norm to identify a small subset of heads that can be trained effectively. For continual learning, we partition heads across tasks to reduce cross-task interference and preserve previously learned capabilities. Theoretically, we relate gradient norm to training effectiveness, and further characterize why sparse, separated head updates can remain stable. Empirically, across math, instruction-following, and coding tasks, tuning higher-ranked heads consistently outperforms tuning lower-ranked ones while often matching denser baselines, and head partitioning improves retention while preserving adaptation to new tasks.

translated_title: 用于稀疏与持续强化学习微调的注意力头排序与划分方法
translated_abstract: 我们通过注意力头的排序与划分来研究语言模型的稀疏与持续强化学习微调。对于稀疏学习，我们按梯度范数对注意力头进行排序，以识别出可以被有效训练的小规模注意力头子集。对于持续学习，我们在不同任务之间划分注意力头，以减少跨任务干扰并保留先前学到的能力。在理论层面，我们将梯度范数与训练效果联系起来，并进一步刻画了为什么稀疏、分离的注意力头更新能够保持稳定。在实证方面，在数学、指令遵循和编程任务上，微调排名较高的注意力头始终优于微调排名较低的注意力头，且通常可与更密集的基线方法相媲美；同时，注意力头划分在保留适应新任务能力的前提下，提升了对旧任务的记忆保持能力。
tldr: 该论文提出按梯度范数对注意力头排序并在任务间划分的方法，实现了语言模型的高效稀疏强化学习微调，同时减少跨任务干扰、提升持续学习中的能力保持。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes ranking attention heads by gradient norm and partitioning them across tasks, enabling efficient sparse reinforcement learning fine-tuning of language models while reducing cross-task interference and improving capability retention in continual learning.
